analysis.title: One Of The Worst Liquidity Sessions In Four Years
key_insights: VIX spot jumped above 28 and closed at its highest level since March, per the GS vol desk (Caroline Warren).
VIX spot sits about 4 vols above the front-month VIX future (ux1), the most inverted VIX term structure since April 2025.
ES1 (S&P 500 e-mini future) top-of-book depth averaged $4.2m on the touch, one of the worst liquidity sessions in four years, which GS says exacerbates price moves.
GS Prime shows the breadth of de-risking as more extreme than the 'Liberation Day' lows (Lib Lows) and the 2022 sell-off.
GS Prime shows a spike in single stock selling that predates this week.
US long/short hedge fund net exposure per MS PB content was 42% coming into the session, a one-year low and the 8th percentile since 2010. Net exposure is expected to be lower after the session.

At current hedge fund net exposure levels, the median historical forecast for next-twelve-month S&P 500 earnings growth is 5% (data since 2016) and at most 10%, against consensus next-year EPS growth of 16%.

Macro systematic strategies are light, with about $25bn to sell over the next week on MS QDS estimates. MS calls this relatively low because leverage was in only the 25th percentile coming into the session.
GS Prime says three years of Momentum exposure build-up has been erased in under 3 months.
Mutual fund managers hold very low cash balances (ICI), which limits dip-buying capacity.
earnings_insights: Per MS QDS, consensus S&P 500 EPS growth for next year is 16% (a consensus estimate). Historical median forecast NTM EPS growth at current hedge fund net exposure levels is 5%, and at most 10%.
risk_factors: Thin futures liquidity (ES1 depth of $4.2m) amplifies price moves.
Hedge fund net exposure will likely fall further after the session.
Systematic funds have about $25bn left to sell over the next week.
Low mutual fund cash limits dip-buying.
Consensus EPS growth of 16% looks high against the 5% to 10% implied by current hedge fund positioning.
